sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Vishakha Pandey, learned counsel holding brief of Shri Ramanuj Tiwari, learned counsel for the petitioners; Shri Fuzail Ahmad Ansari, learned Standing Counsel for State respondents and learned counsel for respondent Nos.2, 3, 8 and 9.
2.

The instant writ petition has been preferred for a direction to respondents to provide the compensation of the acquired land, which was utilized by the respondents under relevant provisions of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
Harshita Khare And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 8 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178327781/
1 2013 in respect of petitioner's land acquired by respondent authority.

entities.text: Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Harshita Khare And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 8 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. Learned Standing Counsel submits that the dispute falls within the jurisdiction of the District Level Committee constituted by the Government Order dated 12.5.2016 and as such no interference is required by this Court in the instant matter at this stage.
4.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits of the issue involved, with the consent of parties herein, the writ petition stands disposed of with observation that in case the petitioner moves a fresh representation ventilating his grievances before the authority concerned constituted under the Government Order dated 12.05.2016 within two weeks, the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law expeditiously, preferably within twelve weeks, thereafter.
